text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like KWEB on 2026-09-18, the median 10-session forward return was 0.68%, but the distribution is wide and right-skewed, with a standard deviation of 8.19%. The single number to anchor on for downside path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -3.3%, which describes the typical intra-horizon drawdown even when the endpoint finished near flat.

[state]
The retrieval engine pulled these 50 analogs because KWEB's current state is defined by extreme distance from its highs and depressed liquidity. The most distinctive features are a distance from 52-week high (dist52) of -42.74% (z-score -1.899) and a 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) of -2.663 (z-score -1.607). These combine with a 20-session return (ret20) of -6.97% and a 20-session return vs benchmark (relBench20) of -7.1%, pulling in other deeply discounted, low-volume names that have recently underperformed. WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) at 19.24% adds an unusual macro signature. The macro regime shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a Fed funds target change over 90 days of 0.25 bp. Equity market sentiment sits at a score of 57.1 in the "Greed" band, though the CNN Business Fear & Greed cross-check reads 38.3 in "fear", driven by extreme fear in stock price strength and breadth. For this specific symbol, Yahoo Finance headlines note "Alibaba Climbs 3%, PDD and JD.com Tick Up: Is China Technology Finding Buyers Again?" and "Trump-Xi Meeting in the Cards: ETFs Currently in Focus". Crypto sentiment is recorded separately at 70 ("Greed") on alternative.me; this applies only to the tokenised wrapper context, not the equity ETF itself.

[history]
Over the 10-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 1.81% and a median of 0.68%. The distribution is heavily right-skewed (skew 2.601), ranging from a minimum of -9.23% to a maximum of 43.14%. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. The 10th percentile outcome was -5.81%, while the 90th percentile was 8.66%. The bad tail is populated by recent sessions: NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -8.41%, PDD on 2026-08-31 returned -7.05%, and NKE on 2026-08-13 returned -6.77%. The closest same-symbol analog, KWEB on 2026-08-31, returned -5.15%. The extreme positive tail is dominated by a single outlier: NIO on 2025-07-08 returned 43.14%. Without that one episode, the upside distribution compresses significantly. The histogram shows the largest concentration of outcomes (18%) clustered around the 0.59% midpoint.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still experience severe intra-horizon pain. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -3.3%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -7.26%, and the 25th percentile was -5.96%. Conversely, the median max favourable excursion was 4.04%, reaching 14.31% at the 90th percentile. Looking at breach probabilities, 32 out of the 50 analogs experienced a 5% drawdown during the 10 sessions. Only 2 analogs breached a 10% drawdown, and none breached 15% or 20%. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 1.22.

[stress]
The baseline median return is 0.68%. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario worsened the median to -9.75% (delta -10.43%), using 48 analogs, with a 75% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario produced a median of -3.36% (delta -4.04%) on 26 analogs, with a 65.4% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario yielded a median of -4.81% (delta -5.49%) on 50 analogs, with a 30% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind showed a median of -2.77% (delta -3.45%) on 36 analogs, with a 22.2% breach probability; caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare median was -3.08% (delta -3.76%) on 50 analogs; caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters late-window analogs. The earnings release day scenario had a median of -1.25% (delta -1.93%) on 50 analogs; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The liquidity air pocket median was -0.51% (delta -1.19%) on 50 analogs; caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue, bounding reference-market gap risk only. The weekend hold on the 7x24 venue scenario produced a median of 0.52% (delta -0.16%) on 50 analogs; caveat: blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count, a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution, and a perpetual carries funding and basis a spot token does not. The vol spike (+2 sigma VIX) median was 0.67% (delta -0.01%) on 50 analogs; caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The crypto drawdown contagion median was 0.78% (delta 0.1%) on 50 analogs; caveat: the BTC feature is a market-wide regime proxy, and any name-level linkage to crypto flows is not identified here. The China ADR de-rating median was 0.49% (delta -0.19%) on 50 analogs; caveat: delisting and audit-access risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space. The FOMC decision day median was 0.2% (delta -0.48%) on 50 analogs; caveat: only 92 decision days exist in the calendar, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. The policy-rate path re-pricing median was -0.41% (delta -1.09%) on 50 analogs; caveat: uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies, and transmission depends on duration and balance sheet, which are not features here. The 2023-03 regional bank stress median was 4.4% (delta 3.72%) on 36 analogs; caveat: very short window, so the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions. No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the 2025-04 tariff shock, because it directly targets China-linked cash flows and produced a -3.36% median with a 65.4% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown across 26 analogs; the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, because it represents the worst historical delta (-10.43%) against the baseline with a 75% breach probability across 48 analogs; and the 2022 inflation/rate bear, because it isolates multiple compression without a credit event, yielding a -4.81% median and a 30% breach probability across 50 analogs. A reader should distrust the heavy year concentration in the retrieval set, where 23 of the 50 analogs originate from 2025 alone, potentially biasing the distribution toward recent regime dynamics. No scenario result contradicts the direction of a neutral-to-cautious read of the baseline distribution, though the 2023-03 regional bank stress and crypto contagion scenarios printed positive medians, reflecting that those specific shocks did not historically impair this type of asset.

[limits]
This analysis is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source. The honest verdict states that analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample (83.6% coverage against an 80% target) and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage (-2.4% matched coverage sharpness vs same name), and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test (chi-square 306.6 vs critical 16.92). The directional hit rate is 49.8%. Regarding path risk validation, at the stated 10% drawdown level, the realised breach rate out of sample was 5.6%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 8.7%, producing a calibration gap of 3.15 percentage points (standard error 1.12). The analog Brier score was 0.0534. Against the volatility reflection benchmark (0.0591), the paired difference confidence interval spans zero (-0.0115 to 0.0004), meaning the comparison is unresolved. Against the same-name calibration (0.0587) and pooled calibration (0.0576) rates, the confidence intervals do not span zero, resolving in favour of the analog. The wrapper status for KWEB on Gate.io is "no-verified-wrapper", meaning no verified tokenised spot figure is reported for that venue. However, the primary venue Bitget is "measured" via the KWEB/USDT RWA perpetual. On Bitget, the reference market is closed for 75.98% of the week, and 68.49% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is classified as a "tight" tracker with a return correlation of 0.9813 and a tracking error of 32 bp/day. The basis band is -0.13% to 0.51%, and the spread is 24.19 bps. Caveat: a tight perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; it carries idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. The return layer measured 6 distinct weekend blocks. The median weekend block return was 0.1215%, the 10th percentile was -0.976%, and the standard deviation was 0.9046%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.331%. Zero percent of these 6 weekends breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
